2609.21327.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Buffered Quantile Objectives
2609.21327.paper_summary: Quantile-based reinforcement learning provides an interpretable approach to risk-sensitive decision-making by optimizing a prescribed quantile of the cumulative-return distribution. Despite this appeal, learning under a point quantile objective is challenging: quantiles can change abruptly under small perturbations of the return distribution, and exact quantile-sensitive planning requires computationally demanding distributional optimization. Lower-buffered quantiles alleviate the former difficulty by averaging neighboring quantiles immediately below the target level, providing a smoother surrogate while preserving the underlying point-quantile objective. Existing methods based on this principle, however, remain model-based and rely on explicit return-law planning, limiting their applicability beyond small tabular problems. We develop Deep-BQRL, a model-free distributional reinforcement-learning framework that extends buffered-quantile learning to neural function approximation. The method learns conditional return quantiles directly from sampled transitions, constructs buffered action scores from the relevant region of the learned quantile function, and uses ensemble disagreement to guide exploration. An augmented input representation allows the learned policy to respond to trajectory information without explicitly reproducing the quantile-state recursion required by exact planning. Experiments on an asset-selling optimal-stopping problem and slippery FrozenLake compare Deep-BQRL with model-based UCB-BQRL and tabular PPO and TRPO implementations. In asset selling, Deep-BQRL attains smaller mean cumulative point-quantile policy gaps than PPO and TRPO at the reported target levels, while UCB-BQRL retains the smallest gaps. The learned stopping decisions also vary with the target quantile, providing an interpretable illustration of the method's risk-sensitive behavior.
2609.21327.paper_summary_zh: 量化基礎的強化學習提供了一種可解釋的風險敏感決策方法，通過優化累積回報分佈的指定分位數來實現。儘管這種方法具有吸引力，但在點分位數目標下進行學習是具有挑戰性的：在回報分佈的小擾動下，分位數可能會突然改變，而精確的分位數敏感規劃需要計算上要求高的分佈優化。低緩衝分位數通過對目標水平下方相鄰的分位數進行平均來緩解前者的困難，提供了一個更平滑的替代方案，同時保留了基本的點分位數目標。然而，基於這一原則的現有方法仍然是基於模型的，並依賴於明確的回報法則規劃，限制了它們在小型表格問題之外的適用性。我們開發了Deep-BQRL，一種無模型的分佈式強化學習框架，將緩衝分位數學習擴展到神經函數逼近。該方法直接從採樣的過渡中學習條件回報分位數，從學習的分位數函數的相關區域構建緩衝行動分數，並利用集成不一致性來指導探索。增強的輸入表示使得學習的策略能夠對軌跡信息作出反應，而無需明確重現精確規劃所需的分位數狀態遞歸。在資產出售的最佳停止問題和滑溜的FrozenLake上進行的實驗中，Deep-BQRL與基於模型的UCB-BQRL以及表格PPO和TRPO實現進行了比較。在資產出售中，Deep-BQRL在報告的目標水平下達到了比PPO和TRPO更小的平均累積點分位數政策差距，而UCB-BQRL保持了最小的差距。學習的停止決策也隨著目標分位數而變化，提供了該方法風險敏感行為的可解釋示例。
